chapters.title: Matrices as transformations
chapters.what: A matrix is a linear map: its columns are where the basis vectors land. Rotations, shears, scalings, reflections and projections are all matrices, and doing one after another is matrix multiplication.
chapters.looks: The grid of the plane (2D) or the lattice of space (3D) is carried along; the unit square becomes a parallelogram of area |det A|, rose-coloured when det < 0 (mirrored).
chapters.change: ▶ morphs from the identity to A; watch a projection squash space flat (det 0).
chapters.use: Every game engine and CAD package; image warping; fonts; robotics; stress and strain.
misc: det 0 means information is lost — no inverse.

examples.world: Stretch ×2 horizontally, squash ×½ vertically: area unchanged.

chapters.title: Linear systems
chapters.what: n linear equations in n unknowns: lines (2D) or planes (3D) that meet in one point, never, or along a line. Gaussian elimination finds which.
chapters.looks: Each equation is a line (2D) or a plane (3D); the solution is where they all meet.
chapters.change: Perturb a right-hand side: well-conditioned systems barely move, ill-conditioned ones swing.
chapters.use: Circuits, structures (truss forces), least squares, every finite-element solve.
misc: Three planes can fail to meet even when no two are parallel.
A zero determinant means no solution OR infinitely many.

chapters.title: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors
chapters.what: An eigenvector is a direction that the matrix only stretches: A v = λ v. The eigenvalues are the stretch factors; they govern growth, vibration, stability and ranking.
chapters.looks: Dashed lines through the origin that the transformation maps onto themselves; everything else turns.
chapters.change: Make the matrix symmetric and the eigen-lines become perpendicular.
chapters.use: Vibration modes, principal stresses and axes of inertia, population growth, Google's PageRank.
misc: A rotation (other than 0° or 180°) has no real eigenvectors in 2D.
Eigenvalues of a product are not products of eigenvalues.

examples.title: A symmetric matrix: perpendicular principal directions
examples.world: Principal stresses, principal axes: [[2, 1], [1, 2]] stretches by 3 along (1, 1) and by 1 along (1, −1).

examples.title: Fibonacci and the golden ratio
examples.world: [[1, 1], [1, 0]] generates Fibonacci numbers; its growth rate is φ = 1.618.

examples.title: PageRank: a web of three pages
examples.world: Google ranked pages by the eigenvector of the link matrix with eigenvalue 1.

examples.title: A Leslie matrix: will the population grow?
examples.world: Age-structured populations grow by the dominant eigenvalue each generation (here 1.284).

examples.title: Principal moments of inertia
examples.world: A body spins steadily about the eigenvectors of its inertia tensor (here 4, 2, 2).

chapters.title: Linear algebra for mechanics
chapters.what: Mechanics is full of matrices: stiffness K u = F, inertia tensors, stress tensors, rotation matrices, and the normal-mode problem K v = ω² M v.
chapters.looks: The same pictures as before, now with physical meaning: the ellipse of stresses, the lines of the modes, the planes of equilibrium.
chapters.change: Stiffen one spring and watch both displacements change — the system is coupled.
chapters.use: Structural analysis, finite elements, vibration, rigid-body dynamics, continuum mechanics.
misc: A stiffness matrix of an unsupported structure is singular (it can move rigidly).
Principal stresses are eigenvalues, not the largest entries.
